Mike Lawrence <Mike.L...@dal.ca> wrote
>
>When a continuous variable is supplied as a mapping to colour, a
>continuous colour scale is used. When a categorical (factored)
>variable is supplied as a mapping to colour, a discrete colour scale
>is used.
>
>These are reasonable/useful defaults and put the onus on the user to
>know the structure of their data.
>

This makes sense. I suppose, then, my question is why the cyl variable is
treated as continuous, but this is clearly not a problem with ggplot2, but
with the data.

>Similarly, ggplot plots categorical (factored) variables in the order
>that they are leveled in the original data. Look at the relev()
>command in the package "ez" for a simple way of re-ordering the levels
>of a factor (if you look at the source, it simply loops relevel() ).
>


Thanks for this. One problem that I (and I imagine others) have is knowing
what to find in which package.


>> p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = as.factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
>> p
>>
>> produces a plot with only three colors of dots, but in the order 6, 4, 8 ...
>
>I don't replicate your observation that the order is 6,4,8; using
>ggplot 0.8.3 I observe the expected order of 4,6,8.
>
>

After I updated ggplot2, I also find the expected order of 4, 6, 8; I should
